rule: Place nc_matmul stationary and moving operands in SBUF and the dst tile in PSUM.
why: The Tensor Engine can only read its inputs from SBUF and only writes its accumulator output to PSUM; any other buffer placement is rejected.
trigger: nc_matmul whose dst is an SBUF/HBM tensor or whose inputs are PSUM/HBM tensors.
fix: Allocate dst with nl.ndarray(..., buffer=nl.psum); stage inputs into SBUF (dma_copy) first; evacuate PSUM with tensor_copy/activation afterwards.
check_sketch: for every nisa.nc_matmul: buffer(stationary)==sbuf and buffer(moving)==sbuf and buffer(dst)==psum

rule: Lay out both nc_matmul operands so the contraction (K) dimension is their partition dimension, with identical partition sizes <= 128.
why: nc_matmul computes dst = stationary.T @ moving; the systolic array contracts along the 128 partition rows, so K must be the partition axis of both tiles.
trigger: Shapes where K is a free dimension, or stationary.shape[0] != moving.shape[0], or partition dim > 128.
fix: Transpose the operand (nc_transpose / dma_transpose / load with transposed access pattern) so K is dim 0; tile K into chunks of <= nl.tile_size.pmax (128) and accumulate.
check_sketch: nc_matmul: stationary.shape[0] == moving.shape[0] <= nl.tile_size.pmax (or <= tile_size[0] when tiling mode is on)
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, sections Layout and Tile size

rule: Keep the free dimension of the nc_matmul stationary operand at most 128 (nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax).
why: The stationary tile is latched into the 128x128 PE array; its free size maps onto the 128 PE columns and becomes the partition dim of dst.
trigger: stationary.shape[1:] product > 128 (e.g. passing a [128, 512] weight tile as stationary).
fix: Tile M (stationary free) into 128-wide chunks, or swap operand roles so the large dimension is the moving free dim (up to 512).
check_sketch: nc_matmul: prod(stationary.shape[1:]) <= nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax (128), or <= tile_size[1] when tiling mode on
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tile size; nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax

rule: On trn1/trn2 keep the nc_matmul moving free dimension at most 512 (nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax).
why: The moving free size equals the dst free size, and one PSUM bank holds 512 fp32 elements per partition (2 KiB); NeuronCore-v2/v3 cannot span banks in one matmul.
trigger: moving free dim > 512 on trn1/trn2 or when the kernel should be portable.
fix: Loop over N in 512-element chunks, each writing its own PSUM region/bank.
check_sketch: nc_matmul on nc_version<=3: prod(moving.shape[1:]) <= nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax (512)
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tile size; nl.tile_size

rule: On trn3 the nc_matmul moving free dimension may go up to 4096 for fp32 dst or 8192 for bf16 dst (entire 8-bank PSUM).
why: NeuronCore-v4 lets a single matmul write across all 8 PSUM banks; bf16 outputs are half the size so twice as many fit.
trigger: Kernels hard-coding 512 moving chunks on trn3 leave throughput on the table; exceeding 4096/8192 fails.
fix: Pick moving chunk size from target: 512 for v2/v3, 4096 (fp32) or 8192 (bf16) for v4; gate with nisa.get_nc_version().
check_sketch: nc_matmul on nc_version==4: prod(moving.shape[1:]) <= (8192 if dst.dtype==bf16 else 4096)

rule: Declare the nc_matmul dst PSUM tile as float32 on trn1/trn2; bf16 dst is only allowed starting trn3.
why: Tensor Engine accumulates in fp32 internally; only NeuronCore-v4 can down-convert to bf16 on PSUM write.
trigger: nl.ndarray(..., dtype=nl.bfloat16, buffer=nl.psum) used as a matmul dst on trn2.
fix: Use dtype=nl.float32 for the PSUM accumulator and cast on the PSUM->SBUF evacuation (tensor_copy/activation casts for free).
check_sketch: nc_matmul: dst.dtype == float32 if nc_version<=3 else dst.dtype in {float32, bfloat16}

rule: Do not mix an fp32/tfloat32 nc_matmul operand with a lower-precision (bf16/fp16/fp8) operand.
why: The PE array runs in a single precision mode per instruction: if either input is fp32/tf32 both must be; other dtypes may be mixed freely.
trigger: stationary bf16 with moving float32 (common when activations stay fp32 and weights are bf16).
fix: Cast one side (tensor_copy / activation with dtype cast) so both are fp32-class or both are <=16-bit; prefer bf16 for 4x PE throughput.
check_sketch: nc_matmul: (stationary.dtype in {fp32,tf32}) == (moving.dtype in {fp32,tf32})

rule: Use only float8_e4m3/float8_e5m2/bfloat16/float16/tfloat32/float32 (plus float8_e4m3fn on trn3) as nc_matmul inputs, and never mix legacy float8_e4m3 with OCP float8_e4m3fn.
why: These are the PE-array native formats; integer tiles are not accepted and the two e4m3 variants have different max values (legacy max 240) so cannot share one instruction.
trigger: int8/int32 tiles passed to nc_matmul, or e4m3 + e4m3fn operands together, or e4m3fn used on trn2.
fix: Quantize/cast to a supported float dtype before the matmul; on trn2 use nl.float8_e4m3 (legacy), on trn3 prefer nl.float8_e4m3fn.
check_sketch: nc_matmul: dtype(op) in allowed set for target; not (e4m3 in dtypes and e4m3fn in dtypes); e4m3fn only if nc_version>=4
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Data types; nki/compiler/target.py comment

rule: Start every PSUM accumulation group with accumulate=False (or accumulate=None) and only then use accumulate=True.
why: accumulate=True adds onto existing PSUM content; on an uninitialized location the result is undefined on all targets. The default None lets the compiler infer first-write-overwrite.
trigger: A K-loop that passes accumulate=True unconditionally, or accumulates into a PSUM tile that was never written by a matmul.
fix: Use accumulate=(k > 0) in the loop, or omit the parameter so the compiler tracks first write.
check_sketch: for each PSUM region: the first nc_matmul writing it must not have accumulate=True literal

rule: Do not memset/tensor_copy a PSUM tile and then accumulate matmuls onto it on trn1/trn2.
why: On NeuronCore-v2/v3 matmul accumulation onto a PSUM location value-initialized by a non-matmul instruction is undefined behavior in hardware.
trigger: nisa.memset(psum_tile, 0) followed by nc_matmul(..., accumulate=True) as a 'bias init' trick.
fix: Let the first matmul overwrite (accumulate=False) and add the bias during PSUM evacuation (activation bias=, tensor_tensor).
check_sketch: flag nc_matmul(accumulate=True) whose dst was last written by memset/tensor_copy and nc_version<=3
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, note under Accumulation mode

rule: Remember nc_matmul computes dst = stationary.T @ moving: stationary free dim becomes dst partition dim, moving free dim becomes dst free dim.
why: Operands are both K-major (K on partitions); the output rows come from the stationary columns, so passing A as stationary yields A.T @ B, not A @ B.
trigger: Mismatched dst shape errors or transposed results when porting A @ B.
fix: For C[M,N] = A[M,K] @ B[K,N]: stationary = A.T tile [K, M<=128], moving = B tile [K, N<=512], dst = [M, N] PSUM.
check_sketch: nc_matmul: dst.shape[0] == prod(stationary.shape[1:]) and prod(dst.shape[1:]) == prod(moving.shape[1:])

rule: When using Tensor Engine tiling mode set both tile_position and tile_size, with start_row a multiple of row_size, column_size == 128 and start_column == 0.
why: Row tiling splits the 128 PE rows into 2x64 (v2+) or 4x32 (v3+) tiles so several small-K matmuls run concurrently; the exposed API currently only allows row tiling.
trigger: Small-K (<=64) matmuls at low PE utilization; or tile_position set without tile_size.
fix: Use tile_size=(64,128)/(32,128) and tile_position=(0|32|64|96, 0) across independent matmuls; keep stationary within the chosen tile.
check_sketch: nc_matmul: (tile_position set) == (tile_size set); tile_size[1]==128; tile_position[1]==0; tile_position[0] % tile_size[0] == 0; tile_size[0] in {32 (v3+),64,128}
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tiling mode and param docs

rule: Use perf_mode=nisa.matmul_perf_mode.double_row only on trn2/trn3 with fp8 operands shaped [K/2, 2, free], never together with column tiling.
why: double_row packs two FP8 pairs per PE for 2x throughput by splitting K between the partition dim and a first free dim of exactly 2.
trigger: double_row on trn1, with bf16 operands, or with first free dim != 2.
fix: Reshape operands to [128, 2, M] / [128, 2, N] fp8 tiles (contraction = 256) and set perf_mode=double_row.
check_sketch: nc_matmul(perf_mode=double_row): nc_version>=3 and dtypes in fp8 set and stationary.shape[1]==2 and moving.shape[1]==2
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, sections Performance mode, Data types, Layout

rule: Set is_stationary_onezero/is_moving_onezero=True when an fp32 operand contains only 0/1 values (masks, one-hot, identity).
why: The hint lets the compiler use a faster fp32 PE path, up to 2x; it has no effect for non-fp32 operands.
trigger: fp32 identity/one-hot/selection matrices used as a matmul operand without the hint.
fix: Add is_stationary_onezero=True (or is_moving_onezero=True) on the one-zero operand.
check_sketch: nc_matmul with fp32 operand built from nl.shared_identity_matrix/ones/iota-compare without onezero hint

rule: Set is_transpose=True for identity-matmul transposes; on trn2+ it is bit-accurate (NaN/Inf preserved), on trn1 it only tags the op for the profiler.
why: NeuronCore-v3+ has a native transpose mode; v2 performs a real fp multiply so NaN/Inf propagate incorrectly.
trigger: Transposing tensors that may hold NaN/Inf on trn1.
fix: On trn1, replace NaN/Inf with finite sentinels before PE transpose, or use Vector Engine nc_transpose for <=32x32 tiles.
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Transpose mode; nki.isa.nc_transpose docstring

rule: Expect each nc_matmul to appear as two ISA instructions in neuron-profile: a stationary load followed by a multiply.
why: The stationary operand is latched into the PE array by a separate load instruction; both show up for a single API call.
trigger: Instruction counts in the profile are ~2x the number of nc_matmul calls; stationary reloads dominate when the stationary tile changes every call.
fix: Keep the stationary operand fixed across consecutive matmuls (loop over moving tiles innermost) to amortize loads.
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Profiler view syntax

rule: When using .indirect() views on nc_matmul operands (trn3), keep tile_position at (0,0), use a Tensor-Engine float dtype, and do not use indirection on moving when is_transpose=True.
why: Tensor indirection (gather/scatter) is incompatible with hardware tiling and only defined for fp16/bf16/fp8 operands.
trigger: nc_matmul with .indirect() plus tile_position/tile_size, or fp32 indirect operands.
fix: Drop tiling mode and cast to bf16/fp16/fp8 when gathering operands; index starts on a 32-partition quadrant boundary.
check_sketch: nc_matmul: any(is_indirect(op)) implies tile_position in {None,(0,0)} and dtype in {fp16,bf16,fp8*} and not (is_transpose and is_indirect(moving))

rule: Explicitly tile any matmul larger than [K<=128] x [M<=128] x [N<=512] into nested loops of nc_matmul calls.
why: nc_matmul maps 1:1 to a hardware instruction and does not auto-tile; shapes beyond the limits are compile errors.
trigger: Calling nc_matmul directly with full-problem tensors.
fix: Loop m in range(0,M,128), n in range(0,N,512), k in range(0,K,128) with PSUM accumulation over k.
check_sketch: nc_matmul operand dims within tile_size limits
source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tile size (final paragraph)

rule: Prefer nisa.nc_matmul with pre-transposed operands over nl.matmul(x, y) with transpose_x=False.
why: nl.matmul is an experimental wrapper; with transpose_x=False it inserts an extra transpose to put x's contraction dim on partitions, costing a PE/Vector pass.
trigger: Hot loops using nl.matmul without transpose_x=True.
fix: Load x already transposed (K on partitions) and call nl.matmul(xT, y, transpose_x=True) or nisa.nc_matmul directly.
check_sketch: nl.matmul call with transpose_x omitted or False

rule: To reduce along the partition axis, either transpose then tensor_reduce, or multiply by a ones[128,1] stationary tile with nc_matmul.
why: Vector Engine reductions only operate on free axes; the Tensor Engine naturally sums across partitions (contraction).
trigger: Attempting nisa.tensor_reduce(axis=0) or looping over partitions.
fix: nc_matmul(dst=psum[1,N], stationary=ones[K,1], moving=data[K,N]) gives column sums; or tensor_partition_reduce on GpSimd.
check_sketch: tensor_reduce with axis containing 0

rule: Only call nisa.nc_matmul_mx and nisa.quantize_mx when targeting trn3 (NeuronCore-v4).
why: MX (microscaling) datapaths exist only in the v4 Tensor and Vector Engines.
trigger: nc_matmul_mx/quantize_mx in a kernel compiled for trn1/trn2.
fix: Guard with nisa.get_nc_version() == nisa.nc_version.gen4 and fall back to bf16 nc_matmul elsewhere.
check_sketch: call to nc_matmul_mx/quantize_mx requires target nc_version>=4

rule: Feed nc_matmul_mx packed x4 operands (float8_e5m2_x4, float8_e4m3fn_x4, float4_e2m1fn_x4) with float8_e8m0fnu scales and an fp32 or bf16 PSUM dst.
why: The MX datapath dequantizes groups of 32 (8 partitions x 4 packed elements) using one shared e8m0 exponent; uint8 scales are only accepted for backward compatibility.
trigger: Unpacked fp8 tiles or fp32 scale tiles passed to nc_matmul_mx.
fix: Produce operands with nisa.quantize_mx (bf16/fp16 -> x4 + e8m0fnu scale) or load pre-packed data via dma_copy.
check_sketch: nc_matmul_mx: dtype(stationary/moving) in x4 set; dtype(scales) in {float8_e8m0fnu, uint8}; dst.dtype in {fp32, bf16}

rule: Shape nc_matmul_mx operands with partition size a multiple of 32 (<=128), an even stationary free size <= 128, and moving free <= 4096 (fp32 dst) or 8192 (bf16 dst).
why: Scale groups span 8-partition blocks inside 32-partition quadrants; column tiling is unavailable so stationary free must fit 128 PE columns.
trigger: Odd stationary free sizes or K tiles of 64 that are not multiples of 32.
fix: Pad K to a multiple of 32 and M to an even number; use row tiling (tile_size=(64|32,128)) for small K.
check_sketch: nc_matmul_mx: shape[0] % 32 == 0 and <= 128; stationary free even and <= 128; moving free <= 4096/8192 by dst dtype

rule: Use only row tiling for nc_matmul_mx: tile_size=(row,128) and tile_position=(start_row,0).
why: The MX datapath supports slicing PE rows (2x64 or 4x32) but not PE columns.
trigger: tile_size with column_size != 128 on nc_matmul_mx.
fix: Set column_size=128, start_column=0.
check_sketch: nc_matmul_mx: tile_size[1]==128 and tile_position[1]==0

rule: Apply .indirect() to an MX data tile and its scale tile together with the same index (or to neither).
why: In MX format data bytes and scale exponents form one logical tensor; gathering one without the other mis-pairs scales.
trigger: stationary.indirect(idx) with a plain stationary_scale.
fix: Use the identical index view on both members of the pair; keep tile_position (0,0).
check_sketch: nc_matmul_mx: is_indirect(stationary)==is_indirect(stationary_scale) with same index; same for moving pair

rule: Give quantize_mx a bf16/fp16 SBUF src with partition size a multiple of 32 (<=128) and free size a multiple of 4; dst free size is src free / 4.
why: Quantization groups are 8 partitions x 4 elements and the x4 output packs four 8-bit values into one 32-bit element.
trigger: Free sizes not divisible by 4 or fp32 inputs.
fix: Cast to bf16 first; pad free dim to a multiple of 4; allocate dst (P, F//4) x4 dtype and dst_scale e8m0fnu in SBUF.
check_sketch: quantize_mx: src.dtype in {bf16,fp16}; src.shape[0]%32==0; prod(src.shape[1:])%4==0; dst free == src free/4; all buffers sbuf
source: nki.isa.quantize_mx docstring, sections Tile size and Scale calculation

rule: Use Tensor Engine nc_transpose only for tiles <= [128,128], reading SBUF and writing PSUM with the same dtype.
why: PE transpose is an identity matmul so it inherits the 128x128 stationary limit and the SBUF-in/PSUM-out rule.
trigger: nc_transpose(engine=tensor) with free dim > 128 or dst in SBUF.
fix: Split into 128x128 blocks; allocate a PSUM dst and evacuate with tensor_copy; multiple free dims are implicitly flattened.
check_sketch: nc_transpose(engine in {tensor,unknown}, shape>32x32): data.shape[0]<=128 and prod(free)<=128 and dst in psum and dst.dtype==data.dtype
source: nki.isa.nc_transpose docstring, sections Memory types and Tile size

rule: Use Vector Engine nc_transpose (engine=nisa.engine.vector) only for tiles <= [32,32]; it may read/write SBUF or PSUM.
why: The Vector Engine transposes within a 32-partition quadrant only.
trigger: engine=vector transpose on a 128x128 tile.
fix: Let engine=unknown pick per shape, or use Tensor Engine for larger tiles.
check_sketch: nc_transpose(engine=vector): data.shape[0]<=32 and prod(free)<=32

rule: Build transpose identities with nl.shared_identity_matrix(n, dtype) rather than ad-hoc constants.
why: The compiler dedupes identity matrices of the same dtype across the graph, saving SBUF and loads.
trigger: Multiple nl.shared_constant(np.eye(...)) or iota-built identities.
fix: ident = nl.shared_identity_matrix(128, dtype=data.dtype); use as moving in nc_matmul(is_transpose=True).
check_sketch: nl.shared_constant with an identity ndarray argument

rule: Only dma_transpose tensors whose dtype is 2 bytes and whose last dim is <= 128, with dst in SBUF and dst.dtype == src.dtype.
why: The DMA transpose path (HWDGE or gather-transpose) moves 2-byte elements and is limited to 128 output partitions.
trigger: dma_transpose on fp32/int8 tensors or on src.shape[-1] > 128.
fix: Cast to bf16/fp16 before transposing, or tile the last dim to <=128; for fp32 use Tensor Engine transpose.
check_sketch: dma_transpose: itemsize(src.dtype)==2 and src.shape[-1]<=128 and buffer(dst)==sbuf and dst.dtype==src.dtype
source: nki.isa.dma_transpose docstring, Direct and Indirect constraints

rule: For HWDGE dma_transpose use src.shape[0]==16 for 2-D input, or shape[0] in {1,2,4,8,16} with (shape[0]*shape[-2]) % 16 == 0 for 3-D/4-D input.
why: The hardware descriptor generator transposes in 16-row blocks.
trigger: 2-D src with 128 rows passed to dma_transpose with dge_mode=hwdge.
fix: Reshape to a 3-D view (16, rows/16, cols) or let dge_mode=unknown choose; for arbitrary shapes use PE transpose.
check_sketch: dma_transpose(dge_mode in {hwdge,unknown}): ndim==2 -> shape[0]==16; ndim in {3,4} -> shape[0] in {1,2,4,8,16} and shape[0]*shape[-2]%16==0
source: nki.isa.dma_transpose docstring, DMA Direct Transpose Constraints

rule: Pass axes as exactly (1,0), (2,1,0) or (3,1,2,0) and give dst the same rank as src with the transposed shape.
why: Only these permutations are implemented; since NKI 0.4.0 a lower-rank dst is an assertion error instead of being silently padded.
trigger: dst 3-D vs src 4-D, or axes=(0,2,1).
fix: Match dst rank to src (e.g. (128,1,1,4096) for a 4-D src) or use a 3-D src with axes=(2,1,0).
check_sketch: dma_transpose: axes in allowed set and dst.ndim==src.ndim and dst.shape==permute(src.shape,axes)

rule: For indirect (gather) dma_transpose on trn2+: src in HBM with shape[0] % 16 == 0, uint32 indices in SBUF with shape[0] in [16,128] divisible by 16 (exactly 128 when indices.shape[1] > 1), dge_mode swdge/unknown.
why: It lowers to a software-DGE dma_gather_transpose that gathers rows by index then transposes.
trigger: Indices in HBM, int32 indices, or 4-D src where both middle dims exceed 1.
fix: Stage indices as nl.uint32 SBUF (128,N); ensure indices.shape[0]*indices.shape[1] >= src.shape[0].
check_sketch: dma_transpose with indices: indices.dtype==uint32 and buffer(indices)==sbuf and 16<=indices.shape[0]<=128 and %16==0 and buffer(src)==hbm
source: nki.isa.dma_transpose docstring, DMA Indirect Transpose Constraints

rule: Budget for 7 usable PSUM banks (not 8) when the compiler lowers dma_transpose to a PE transpose on trn2+.
why: nl.tile_size.psum_num_banks returns 7 when NKI_DMA_TRANSPOSE_AS_PE_TRANSPOSE lowering is active because bank 7 is reserved for nc_transpose.
trigger: Manual PSUM address planning that assumes 8 banks fails or collides.
fix: Read nl.tile_size.psum_num_banks inside the kernel instead of hard-coding 8.
check_sketch: manual PSUM address >= 7*2048 while dma_transpose lowering is enabled

rule: Never dma_copy directly out of PSUM; copy PSUM to SBUF with tensor_copy/activation first.
why: Since NKI 0.3.0 DMA engines cannot read PSUM; the DMA path only connects HBM and SBUF.
trigger: nisa.dma_copy(dst=hbm, src=psum_tile) after a matmul.
fix: sb = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.tensor_copy(dst=sb, src=psum); nisa.dma_copy(dst=hbm, src=sb).
check_sketch: dma_copy: buffer(src) != psum and buffer(dst) != psum
source: migration/index.rst section 'nisa.dma_copy - reading from PSUM'; nki.isa.dma_copy docstring Memory types

rule: For SBUF-to-SBUF movement prefer nisa.tensor_copy (or nc_n_gather/local_gather for gathers) over dma_copy.
why: DMA engines have higher latency and are shared bandwidth; on-chip engines move data within SBUF without descriptors.
trigger: dma_copy where both src and dst are SBUF tiles.
fix: Replace with nisa.tensor_copy(dst, src) (engine chosen by compiler) or a gather instruction.
check_sketch: dma_copy with buffer(src)==sbuf and buffer(dst)==sbuf
source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring, section Memory types; nki.isa.nc_n_gather docstring

rule: Make src and dst of dma_copy have identical total element counts (shapes may differ).
why: DMA moves a flat stream of elements described by two access patterns; mismatched counts are rejected.
trigger: Copying a (128,512) tile into a (128,256) destination slice.
fix: Slice both sides to the same count; use .ap()/reshape views for layout changes.
check_sketch: dma_copy: prod(src.shape)==prod(dst.shape)

rule: Expect dma_copy with differing dtypes to cast src->fp32->dst, except under dge_mode=hwdge where dtypes must match exactly.
why: Static/SW-DGE DMAs have cast logic; HWDGE moves raw bytes without interpreting data.
trigger: dma_copy(dst=bf16, src=fp32, dge_mode=hwdge) fails validation.
fix: Use dge_mode=none/swdge for casting copies, or .view(dtype) to reinterpret bytes under hwdge.
check_sketch: dma_copy(dge_mode==hwdge): src.dtype==dst.dtype
source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring Data types; migration/index.rst 'dge_mode type matching'

rule: Choose dge_mode deliberately: none (runtime pre-generated descriptors, static addresses only), swdge (GpSimd generates, needed for gather/scatter), hwdge (Sync/Scalar sequencer, trn2+, dynamic start address).
why: Dynamic (register/SBUF-dependent) addresses cannot use pre-generated descriptors; only swdge supports per-partition vector indices; hwdge costs no GpSimd time.
trigger: Indirect dma_copy with dge_mode=none, or hwdge requested on trn1.
fix: Leave dge_mode=unknown unless profiling shows GpSimd is a bottleneck, then move static/scalar-offset copies to hwdge with engine=sync or scalar.
check_sketch: dma_copy: vector_offset used -> dge_mode in {swdge,unknown}; hwdge -> nc_version>=3
source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring, DGE modes paragraph and params

rule: Pass engine=nisa.engine.sync or nisa.engine.scalar to dma_copy only together with dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge.
why: The engine field selects which sequencer drives the hardware DGE; it is meaningless for swdge/none.
trigger: dma_copy(engine=scalar) without hwdge.
fix: Add dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge or drop engine.
check_sketch: dma_copy: engine != unknown implies dge_mode == hwdge and engine in {sync, scalar}

rule: Set oob_mode=nisa.oob_mode.skip on indirect dma_copy/dma_compute/dma_transpose when indices may legitimately exceed bounds (e.g. padded expert tables).
why: Dynamic DMAs enable bounds checking; the default oob_mode.error raises a runtime error instead of silently skipping.
trigger: MoE/gather kernels failing at runtime with OOB DMA errors.
fix: Add oob_mode=nisa.oob_mode.skip, or clamp indices before the copy.

rule: Use the DMA priority (0-3, lower is higher priority) argument only on trn3.
why: DMA QoS levels are a NeuronCore-v4 feature; earlier targets reject or ignore it.
trigger: priority= passed to dma_copy/collectives on trn2.
fix: Gate priority usage on nisa.get_nc_version()==gen4.
check_sketch: priority is not None implies nc_version>=4
source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring, param priority; nki.collectives docstrings

rule: For gather/scatter dma_copy use .ap(pattern, vector_offset=idx, indirect_dim=0) on the HBM tensor, with idx an SBUF (P,1) tensor; only indirect_dim=0 is supported.
why: Vector indirection gives each of the P partitions its own row index; the stride on the indirect dim is taken from the base tensor shape, not the pattern.
trigger: vector_offset applied to an SBUF tensor, idx in HBM, or indirect_dim=1.
fix: Load indices into SBUF (P,1) int32/uint32 first; put the indirected tensor (HBM) on the side with .ap(); set pattern stride of dim 0 to prod(base.shape[1:]).
check_sketch: ap(vector_offset=...): buffer(self)==hbm and buffer(vector_offset)==sbuf and vector_offset.shape[1]==1 and indirect_dim==0
source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring, Indirect addressing; migration/index.rst 'Vector dynamic access'

rule: For a dynamic uniform offset use .ap(pattern, scalar_offset=reg_or_1x1_sbuf, indirect_dim=N); the element offset added is scalar_offset * prod(base.shape[N+1:]).
why: indirect_dim is relative to the base tensor, not the pattern; the scalar may be a 1x1 SBUF tensor or a VirtualRegister.
trigger: Off-by-stride bugs when the pattern shape differs from the base shape.
fix: Compute offsets against base tensor shape; vector_offset and scalar_offset are mutually exclusive.
check_sketch: ap(): not (scalar_offset and vector_offset)

rule: Do not pass dst_rmw_op/unique_indices to dma_copy; use nisa.dma_compute(dst, [src, dst], reduce_op=nl.add) for read-modify-write.
why: DMA RMW moved to dma_compute in NKI 0.3.0; dma_copy no longer accepts those parameters.
trigger: Old scatter-add loops using dma_copy(dst_rmw_op=nl.add).
fix: First iteration dma_copy; later iterations dma_compute(dst=acc, srcs=[src.ap(...), acc], reduce_op=nl.add, unique_indices=True).
check_sketch: dma_copy kwargs contain dst_rmw_op or unique_indices

rule: Use dma_compute only with reduce_op=nl.add, scales all 1.0/None, <= 16 sources of identical element count, and for scatter/gather RMW exactly 2 sources with unique_indices=True.
why: Current DMA compute logic supports only summation; RMW uses SW DGE while plain dma_compute uses static DMA (compiler assigns).
trigger: dma_compute with nl.maximum, non-unit scales, or 3 sources with vector_offset.
fix: Pre-scale in SBUF with tensor_scalar; split into pairwise adds.
check_sketch: dma_compute: reduce_op==add and all(s==1.0) and len(srcs)<=16 and (vector_offset present -> len(srcs)==2 and unique_indices)

rule: .ap(pattern=[[stride,count],...]) overrides shape/strides entirely; list the partition dim first for on-chip tensors and keep counts consistent with the instruction's expected element count.
why: It is the as_strided-style escape hatch; the compiler trusts the pattern and the offset composes with the view's base offset.
trigger: Patterns with mismatched element totals or partition dim not first.
fix: Start from t.get_pattern() and edit strides; pass offset explicitly when shifting.
check_sketch: ap(): len(pattern)>=1 and pattern[0][1] <= 128 for sbuf/psum

rule: Treat nl.load/nl.store as experimental conveniences; for control and portability write nisa.dma_copy(dst=..., src=...) with explicit SBUF tiles.
why: nl.load/store were removed in 0.2.0 and reintroduced in 0.3.0 as wrappers that allocate the SBUF tile for you; nisa.dma_copy exposes dge_mode/oob/priority.
trigger: Kernels mixing nl.load with manual allocation/scheduling needs.
fix: sb = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.dma_copy(dst=sb, src=hbm[...]).
source: nki.language.load/store docstrings (<<experimental>>); migration/index.rst note on nl.load/nl.store

rule: Route activation functions (exp, gelu, sigmoid, ...) through nisa.activation/activate2 on the Scalar Engine; math is always fp32 internally with free output casting.
why: Scalar Engine evaluates piecewise-polynomial activations with fused scale/bias and optional free-dim reduce; input is upcast to fp32 and dst cast is free.
trigger: Elementwise exp/tanh done via tensor_tensor/tensor_scalar on Vector Engine or via nl.* wrappers in a Vector-bound kernel.
fix: nisa.activation(dst, op=nl.exp, data, scale=s, bias=b, reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_res=rowsum) fuses scale, bias, exp and row-sum in one instruction.

rule: Give activation a float32 scale (scalar or [N,1] vector) and a bias that is an [N,1] vector on trn1 (scalar allowed from trn2) of any dtype except tfloat32.
why: Scale/bias are broadcast along the free dim per partition; NeuronCore-v2 lacks scalar-bias immediates.
trigger: bias=0.5 scalar on trn1; scale tile in bf16; bias shape (1,N).
fix: Allocate bias as nl.ndarray((N,1), ...) in SBUF; keep scale fp32.
check_sketch: activation: scale is const or (shape==(N,1) and dtype==fp32); bias scalar -> nc_version>=3; bias.dtype != tfloat32; N==data.shape[0]
source: nki.isa.activation docstring, sections Data types and Layout

rule: Make activation/activate2 data and dst share the same partition size (<=128) and the same number of elements per partition.
why: The instruction is a per-lane streaming op; shapes may differ but element counts per partition must match.
trigger: dst (128,512) with data (128,2,256) is fine; dst (128,256) with data (128,512) is rejected.
fix: Reshape views rather than changing element counts.
check_sketch: activation: data.shape[0]==dst.shape[0]<=128 and prod(data.shape[1:])==prod(dst.shape[1:])

rule: Keep inputs of Scalar Engine log/sin/arctan/sqrt/rsqrt/reciprocal within their valid ranges (log [2^-64,2^64], sin [-pi,pi], arctan [-pi/2,pi/2], sqrt [2^-116,2^118], rsqrt [2^-87,2^97], reciprocal +-[2^-42,2^42]); use nl.sin for unbounded sine.
why: Activations are polynomial fits with no range reduction or clamping; e.g. nisa.activation(op=nl.sin) on 9.0 returns ~27.65. nl.sin adds range-reduction instructions.
trigger: Rotary/positional kernels feeding raw angles to nisa.activation(op=nl.sin); log of 0; reciprocal of tiny denominators.
fix: Reduce arguments modulo 2*pi (or call nl.sin), clamp with tensor_scalar max/min, or add epsilon before log/rsqrt.
check_sketch: activation(op in {sin,arctan,log,sqrt,rsqrt,reciprocal}) without preceding range reduction/clamp

rule: Use only the Scalar Engine activation set as activation op: copy, square, sigmoid, relu, prelu, gelu, gelu_dx, gelu_apprx_tanh, gelu_apprx_sigmoid, gelu_apprx_sigmoid_dx, silu, silu_dx, tanh, softplus, mish, erf, erf_dx, exp, log, sin, arctan, sqrt, rsqrt, reciprocal, sign, abs.
why: Only these have hardware polynomial tables; other nl ops (e.g. nl.cos, nl.tan, nl.power) are not activation ops.
trigger: nisa.activation(op=nl.cos) or op=nl.power.
fix: Compose from supported ops (cos via sin(x+pi/2) with range reduction; power via exp(y*log(x)) on valid ranges) or use tensor_tensor(op=nl.power) on GpSimd.
check_sketch: activation.op in ACT_FUNCS

rule: When a Scalar Engine instruction writes through a .indirect() scatter view, the dst must be in SBUF, not PSUM.
why: Scalar Engine scatter writes are only wired to SBUF on NeuronCore-v4.
trigger: activation/tensor_scalar(engine=scalar)/tensor_copy(engine=scalar) with dst.indirect(idx) in PSUM.
fix: Scatter into an SBUF tile, or run the op on Vector Engine.
check_sketch: scalar-engine op: is_indirect(dst) implies buffer(dst)==sbuf

rule: Use nisa.activate2 only on trn3 and only with (op0,op1) in {(multiply,add),(multiply,subtract),(multiply,bypass),(add,bypass),(subtract,bypass),(bypass,bypass)}.
why: activate2 is the NeuronCore-v4 three-stage Scalar pipeline (tensor-scalar, activation, reduce); other combos have no encoding.
trigger: activate2 with op0=nl.add, op1=nl.multiply, or activate2 on trn2.
fix: Reorder as (multiply, add) with reverse flags, or fall back to tensor_scalar + activation.
check_sketch: activate2: nc_version>=4 and (op0,op1) in ALLOWED6; op1 set -> op0 set; reverse0 -> op0 set; reverse1 -> op1 set

rule: Prefer nisa.activation(reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_cmd=nisa.reduce_cmd.reset_reduce, reduce_res=...) over nisa.activation_reduce.
why: activation_reduce is kept only for backward compatibility and is equivalent to activation with reset_reduce.
trigger: New code calling nisa.activation_reduce.
fix: Replace with nisa.activation(..., reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_cmd=nisa.reduce_cmd.reset_reduce, reduce_res=out).
check_sketch: call to nisa.activation_reduce

rule: Use reduce_op=nl.add for nisa.activation's fused reduction; the richer set (add, maximum, minimum, abs_max, abs_min) is only available through activate2 on trn3.
why: The legacy activation instruction only has a summing reduce path; v4's activate2 adds max/min variants.
trigger: activation(reduce_op=nl.maximum) to compute a row max on trn2.
fix: Compute row max with tensor_reduce(op=nl.maximum) or range_select/select_reduce on Vector Engine.
check_sketch: activation: reduce_op in {None, add}; activate2: reduce_op in {add,maximum,minimum,abs_max,abs_min}
source: nki.isa.activation docstring ('reduce_op must be nl.add'); nki.isa.activate2 docstring

rule: Do not pass a bias to nisa.activation(op=nl.reciprocal) on trn1.
why: NeuronCore-v2 Scalar Engine reciprocal lacks bias support.
trigger: activation(op=nl.reciprocal, bias=eps) on trn1.
fix: Add epsilon with tensor_scalar first, or use nisa.reciprocal on Vector Engine.
check_sketch: activation(op==reciprocal) and bias is not None and nc_version==2

rule: Treat the Scalar Engine's 128 reduce registers as shared mutable state across all activation/activate2/activation_reduce calls; reset with reset_reduce before each new reduction chain and do not interleave activation_reduce with activation chains.
why: There is one 32-bit accumulator per lane shared by all Scalar reduce-capable instructions; reduce_regs persist until reset.
trigger: Interleaved softmax row sums from two independent streams producing wrong totals.
fix: Start each chain with reduce_cmd=reset_reduce, continue with reduce, pass reduce_res only on the last call (extra readout instruction costs a little).
check_sketch: activation chain: first call reduce_cmd==reset_reduce; no activation_reduce between reduce and final readout

rule: Treat Vector Engine accumulators as shared across exponential, range_select, select_reduce, tensor_scalar_reduce and tensor_scalar_cumulative; always issue reset_reduce after any instruction that ran with reduce_cmd=idle.
why: Even idle-mode instructions may clobber the accumulator state, so continuing with reduce after them yields garbage.
trigger: Flash-attention loops mixing range_select(reduce) with unrelated select_reduce(idle).
fix: Use reduce_cmd=reset_reduce at the start of each accumulation group and reduce for continuation; avoid interleaving other accumulating ops.
check_sketch: vector accumulating op with reduce_cmd==reduce preceded by a vector accumulating op with reduce_cmd==idle
source: nki.isa.exponential, select_reduce, tensor_scalar_reduce docstrings (Accumulator behavior notes)

rule: In tensor_scalar_reduce use one arithmetic op0, reduce_op in {add, multiply, max, min}, pass reduce_init only with load_reduce, and do not rely on reverse0 (unsupported).
why: Only one ALU stage exists before the reduce path; identity init is 0/1/-inf/+inf per reduce_op.
trigger: tensor_scalar_reduce(op0=..., op1=...) or reverse0=True.
fix: Chain a tensor_scalar first if two ops are needed; use reduce_cmd=load_reduce with reduce_init for warm starts.
check_sketch: tensor_scalar_reduce: reduce_op in {add,multiply,maximum,minimum}; reduce_init set iff reduce_cmd==load_reduce; reverse0==False

rule: Do not use int32/uint32 tiles as input or output of tensor_scalar_cumulative; op1 must be add/subtract/mult/max/min.
why: ISA limitation of the cumulative path; 32-bit integers are not representable in its fp32 datapath.
trigger: Cumulative sums over int32 index arrays.
fix: Compute in fp32/int16 and cast, or use iota-based arithmetic.
check_sketch: tensor_scalar_cumulative: dtype(src/dst) not in {int32,uint32}; op1 in {add,subtract,multiply,maximum,minimum}

rule: Never give tensor_tensor, tensor_tensor_scan or scalar_tensor_tensor two PSUM inputs; at most one of the two tensor operands may live in PSUM.
why: Vector Engine has a single PSUM read port per instruction.
trigger: Adding two matmul accumulators directly from PSUM.
fix: Evacuate one operand to SBUF with tensor_copy first, or accumulate both matmuls into one PSUM tile.
check_sketch: tensor_tensor/scan/stt: not (buffer(a)==psum and buffer(b)==psum)

rule: For per-partition scalar/vector broadcasts use tensor_scalar (or scalar_tensor_tensor), not a broadcast view into tensor_tensor.
why: tensor_tensor requires identical element counts per partition and is slower; tensor_scalar broadcasts a (P,1) operand along the free dim at no extra cost and can fuse two ops.
trigger: nisa.tensor_tensor(data1=x, data2=rowmax.broadcast(1,N), op=nl.subtract).
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(dst, x, nl.subtract, rowmax[(P,1)]) or scalar_tensor_tensor for (x*s)+y.
check_sketch: tensor_tensor where one operand is a broadcast view
source: nki.isa.tensor_tensor docstring (note on broadcasting); nki.isa.tensor_scalar docstring

rule: Expect tensor_tensor on all-int32/uint32 tiles to run on GpSimd (exact integer math) unless an operand is in PSUM or engine=vector is forced; nl.power always runs on GpSimd.
why: Vector Engine casts through fp32 and loses precision above 2^24; GpSimd has native integer ALUs but cannot touch PSUM.
trigger: Index arithmetic giving wrong results after forcing engine=vector; power op with PSUM operands failing.
fix: Keep int32 index math in SBUF; avoid PSUM operands for power/int32 ops.
check_sketch: tensor_tensor(op==power or all int32): no operand in psum

rule: Fuse two broadcast ops into one tensor_scalar call ((data op0 operand0) op1 operand1); one op costs the same as two.
why: The Vector/Scalar/GpSimd ALU pipeline has two stages per element regardless of use.
trigger: Back-to-back tensor_scalar(multiply) then tensor_scalar(add) on the same tile.
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(dst, x, nl.multiply, s, op1=nl.add, operand1=b).
check_sketch: two consecutive tensor_scalar on same tile each with op1=None

rule: Make tensor_scalar operand0/operand1 either compile-time constants or (data.shape[0],1) fp32 tiles; for unary op0 (abs, rsqrt) pass operand0=None or 0.
why: The broadcast operand is read as a per-partition fp32 immediate.
trigger: operand0 as a bf16 (P,1) tile or an (1,N) row vector.
fix: Cast the per-partition vector to fp32 (tensor_copy) and shape it (P,1).
check_sketch: tensor_scalar: operand tiles have shape (P,1) and dtype fp32

rule: In tensor_scalar use bitvec ops only on Vector Engine with integer dtypes; on trn2 the Scalar Engine only accepts (multiply,add), (multiply,None), (add,None); engine=gpsimd is only allowed for rsqrt.
why: Each engine implements a subset of ALU ops; both ops in one instruction must be the same class (bitvec or arithmetic).
trigger: tensor_scalar(op0=nl.maximum, engine=scalar) on trn2; bitwise_and on bf16 data.
fix: Leave engine=unknown, or move clamps to Vector Engine.
check_sketch: tensor_scalar: class(op0)==class(op1); bitvec -> engine in {vector,unknown} and int dtypes; engine==scalar and nc_version==3 -> (op0,op1) in {(mul,add),(mul,None),(add,None)}; engine==gpsimd -> op0==rsqrt

rule: Reduce only over the trailing contiguous free axes with tensor_reduce/nl.sum/nl.max etc. (e.g. (3,), (2,3), (1,2,3) for a 4-D tile); axis 0 is never reducible.
why: Vector Engine reduces along the innermost free dims per partition; since 0.3.0 axis numbers refer to real tensor dims (axis=1 no longer means 'last').
trigger: nl.sum(x, axis=1) on a 3-D tile, or axis=0.
fix: Rearrange the tile so the reduced dims are last, or transpose for partition reductions.
check_sketch: reduce axis tuple == range(k, ndim) for some k>=1
source: nki.isa.tensor_reduce docstring; nl.sum/mean/max docstrings; migration/index.rst tensor_reduce axis fix

rule: Use tensor_reduce(negate=True) to get -sum for free instead of a separate negate; bitvec reductions require integer dtypes and skip casting.
why: The negate multiplies by -1 in the output stage at no cost; bitvec ops treat elements as raw bits.
trigger: A tensor_scalar(multiply,-1) after a reduce; bitwise_or reduce on fp tiles.
fix: Pass negate=True (arithmetic ops only); cast to int for bitvec reductions.
check_sketch: tensor_reduce(bitvec op) -> int dtypes

rule: Size the tensor_reduce dst so elements per partition equal the product of the non-reduced free dims (1 when all free dims are reduced); use keepdims=True to keep broadcastable shape.
why: The instruction writes exactly one result per surviving free index per partition.
trigger: dst (128,512) for a full-free reduction of (128,512) data.
fix: dst = nl.ndarray((P,1), ...) or keepdims=True.
check_sketch: tensor_reduce: prod(dst.shape[1:]) == prod(data.shape[1:k])

rule: Use nisa.tensor_partition_reduce (GpSimd) for cross-partition add/average/max/bitwise_or/bitwise_and reductions when a matmul-based reduction is not suitable.
why: GpSimd can reduce across its 16-partition groups; Vector Engine cannot reduce axis 0.
trigger: Looping over partitions with tensor_tensor adds.
fix: nisa.tensor_partition_reduce(dst, nl.add, data) (SBUF only, GpSimd cannot read PSUM).
check_sketch: tensor_partition_reduce: buffers sbuf

rule: Keep every GpSimd Engine instruction (iota, affine_select, nc_n_gather, local_gather, tensor_partition_reduce, nonzero_with_count, topk, sequence_bounds, rng/rand_get_state with engine=gpsimd, tensor_copy/memset/tensor_tensor on gpsimd) on SBUF operands only.
why: GpSimd has no PSUM port; the compiler falls back to Vector where it can (int32 tensor_tensor) or errors.
trigger: iota or affine_select writing a PSUM tile; tensor_copy(engine=gpsimd) from PSUM.
fix: Target SBUF tiles; evacuate PSUM with Vector/Scalar tensor_copy first.
check_sketch: op.engine==gpsimd implies all operand buffers == sbuf

rule: Pick tensor_copy's engine deliberately: Scalar casts via fp32 (lossy for int32 and unsupported on trn1 - use activation(op=nl.copy) there), Vector/GpSimd are bit-accurate when dtypes match, and PSUM operands require Vector or Scalar.
why: Three engines implement copy with different casting behaviour and memory ports.
trigger: tensor_copy of int32 ids on Scalar Engine corrupting values > 2^24; tensor_copy(engine=scalar) on trn1.
fix: Use engine=vector for exact int copies; use nisa.activation(op=nl.copy) for Scalar copies on trn1.
check_sketch: tensor_copy(engine==scalar): nc_version>=3 and not (int32 dtype); any psum operand -> engine in {vector,scalar,unknown}

rule: Call memset with a value literal of the destination dtype (int literal for int tiles) and value=0 only for x4 packed dtypes; engine may be vector or gpsimd.
why: Since 0.3.0 the value type is strictly validated; the ISA memset writes one u32 pattern so packed sub-elements cannot be set to non-zero.
trigger: memset(int32_tile, 2.0); memset(fp8_x4_tile, 1).
fix: memset(buf, 2); for non-zero x4 data load precomputed values with dma_copy.
check_sketch: memset: type(value) matches dst.dtype class; dst.dtype endswith _x4 -> value==0

rule: Write iota and affine_select outputs to SBUF (partition <= 128) with a pattern whose total element count equals elements per partition; iota values are int32-computed, affine_select on_false_value must be float32.
why: Both run on GpSimd, generate an affine value per element from [[step,num],...] (<=4-D) and cast to dst dtype.
trigger: Causal mask via affine_select into PSUM; pattern [[1,512]] for a (128,1024) dst.
fix: dst in SBUF; pattern product == prod(dst.shape[1:]); cast on write via dst dtype.
check_sketch: iota/affine_select: buffer(dst)==sbuf and prod(num in pattern)==prod(dst.shape[1:]) and len(pattern)<=4

rule: Use range_select (trn2+) with on_false_value=FP32_MIN (-3.4028235e+38), fp32 (P,1) bounds, comp ops in {equal, less, less_equal, greater, greater_equal}, reduce_op=nl.maximum, and range_start + free index < 2^24.
why: The hardware fill value is fixed and comparisons run in fp32 so indices must be exactly representable.
trigger: range_select(on_false_value=-1e9) or on tiles wider than 2^24 columns offset.
fix: Keep the default on_false_value; cast bounds to fp32 (P,1).
check_sketch: range_select: on_false_value==-3.4028235e+38; bound dtypes fp32 and shape (P,1); nc_version>=3

rule: When range_select writes a bf16/fp16/fp8 dst, keep reduce_res in fp32 so a fully-masked row (-inf after downcast) does not produce NaN in the following activation subtract.
why: FP32_MIN downcasts to -inf; activation upcasts to fp32 so (-inf) - FP32_MIN = -inf and exp(-inf)=0, but if reduce_res is also -inf you get -inf - (-inf) = NaN.
trigger: NaNs in masked attention rows with bf16 scores.
fix: reduce_res = nl.ndarray((P,1), nl.float32, buffer=nl.sbuf).
check_sketch: range_select: dst.dtype != fp32 implies reduce_res.dtype == fp32
source: nki.isa.range_select docstring, note on numerical stability

rule: For select_reduce/tensor_copy_predicated keep predicate in an integer dtype (uint8/int8/uint16/int16; uint32 allowed for predicated copy), identical shapes, at most one of on_true/predicate in PSUM, scalar on_false as fp32, and reduce_op=max only.
why: Vector Engine predicate path reads integer masks and has a single PSUM port.
trigger: Float 0/1 masks passed as predicate; both predicate and on_true from PSUM.
fix: Produce masks with comparison ops using dtype=nl.uint8; evacuate one PSUM operand.
check_sketch: select_reduce: predicate.dtype in int set; not(both psum); on_true.dtype not in {tfloat32,int32,uint32}; reduce_op==maximum

rule: On trn3 use nisa.exponential(dst, src, max_value=rowmax, reduce_res=rowsum, reduce_cmd=reset_reduce) on Vector Engine for softmax instead of activation(op=nl.exp).
why: The dedicated v4 Vector instruction fuses max subtraction and running sum and is faster than the Scalar activation path, also balancing engine load.
trigger: Softmax on trn3 still using Scalar exp for exp+sum.
fix: Guard with get_nc_version()==gen4; keep activation path for trn1/trn2.
check_sketch: exponential: nc_version>=4; reduce_init==0 unless reduce_cmd==load_reduce

rule: Use Vector nisa.reciprocal for small tiles (<64 elements/partition) or when precision matters; use Scalar activation(op=nl.reciprocal) for large tiles (about 8x throughput).
why: Vector costs max(MIN_II, 8N) cycles vs Scalar max(MIN_II, N) with MIN_II ~64 cycles; Vector is more precise.
trigger: Hot full-width reciprocal on Vector Engine; precision issues from Scalar reciprocal.
fix: Switch engine per tile size; combine with activation scale/bias fusion.

rule: Choose rsqrt engine deliberately: GpSimd (tensor_scalar(op0=nl.rsqrt, operand0=0.0, engine=gpsimd) / nl.rsqrt) is more precise but 4x slower than Scalar activation(op=nl.rsqrt); nl.rsqrt no longer accepts PSUM inputs.
why: Since 0.5.0 nl.rsqrt runs on GpSimd which has no PSUM access.
trigger: nl.rsqrt(psum_tile) compile failure; layernorm rsqrt on GpSimd becoming the bottleneck.
fix: Evacuate to SBUF first or call nisa.activation(op=nl.rsqrt) directly.
check_sketch: nl.rsqrt arg buffer != psum

rule: Feed bn_stats at most 512 elements per partition (nl.tile_size.bn_stats_fmax) and aggregate the 6-element outputs of several calls with one bn_aggr whose input length per partition is a multiple of 3.
why: Hardware limit of the Vector Engine statistics unit; bn_stats emits (count, mean, var*count) pairs for even/odd elements.
trigger: LayerNorm over D=1024 in one bn_stats call.
fix: Loop over 512-element slices writing bn_stats outputs to offsets in one SBUF tensor, then bn_aggr once.
check_sketch: bn_stats: prod(data.shape[1:]) <= nl.tile_size.bn_stats_fmax (512); bn_aggr: prod(data.shape[1:]) % 3 == 0

rule: For nisa.dropout keep dst.dtype == data.dtype and use an fp32 prob when data is integer.
why: The Vector Engine dropout path preserves dtype and reads probabilities as floats.
trigger: dropout casting bf16->fp32 in one call.
fix: Cast separately; prob scalar or (P,1) tile.
check_sketch: dropout: dst.dtype==data.dtype; data int -> prob.dtype==fp32

rule: Use nc_stream_shuffle only within 32-partition quadrants: same dtype and elements per partition, 32-entry mask (255 = keep), and start partitions 0 (96/128 active), 0/64 (64 active) or 0/32/64/96 (32 active).
why: Vector Engine cross-partition movement is limited to a quadrant with fixed base alignment.
trigger: Shuffling partition 10 to 40, or src starting at partition 16.
fix: Align tiles to quadrant boundaries; for arbitrary partition moves use a PE transpose/matmul with a permutation matrix.
check_sketch: nc_stream_shuffle: len(mask)==32; start partitions in allowed set for ceil(max(P)/32)*32

rule: Give max8/nc_find_index8/nc_match_replace8 between 8 and 16384 elements per partition; outputs are exactly 8 per partition (find_index8 uint32 default, sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF when absent).
why: Fixed-width top-8 hardware path on Vector Engine.
trigger: Top-k over 32768 columns in one call.
fix: Split into <=16384-column chunks and merge the 8-wide results; or use nisa.topk on GpSimd.
check_sketch: max8/find_index8: 8 <= prod(src.shape[1:]) <= 16384; dst.shape[1]==8

rule: Do not assume nc_match_replace8 and nc_find_index8 order duplicate matches the same way: match_replace8 pairs duplicates in descending position order across dst_idx columns, find_index8 in ascending order.
why: The two instructions process vals in opposite directions (match_replace8 iterates i=7..0).
trigger: Top-k index extraction that mixes the two instructions giving permuted indices.
fix: Use one instruction consistently or sort indices afterwards.

rule: Use nisa.topk with BF16 SBUF src in 16-partition snake layout, partition dim multiple of 16, 8 <= n < 65536, 1 <= K < 32768, K <= n, src free >= ceil(n/16); cost ~4n+K GpSimd cycles per partition.
why: GpSimd top-k reads a snake of n BF16 values across 16 partitions.
trigger: fp32 inputs or n > 65535.
fix: Cast to bf16 and reshape into the snake layout; derive K from val_dst free dim.
check_sketch: topk: src.dtype==bf16; val_dst bf16; idx_dst uint32; shape[0]%16==0; 8<=n<65536; 1<=K<32768; K<=n; src.shape[1]>=ceil(n/16)

rule: Expect nonzero_with_count (trn2+) to read and write only partitions 0,16,...,112; dst needs one extra free element (count) and int32 dtype, src fp32/int32 in SBUF.
why: Each GpSimd core touches only the first of its 16 connected partitions.
trigger: Reading results from partitions other than multiples of 16.
fix: Place one row per 16-partition group or replicate inputs; read dst[k*16, :].
check_sketch: nonzero_with_count: dst.shape[1]==src.shape[1]+1; dst.dtype==int32; src.dtype in {fp32,int32}; nc_version>=3

rule: For local_gather use uint16 indices, src_buffer.shape[0]==index.shape[0] with a multiple of 16, num_elem_per_idx in {1,2,4,8,16,32}, and <= 4096 indices per GpSimd core; indices are partition offsets within each 16-partition group.
why: Each of 8 GpSimd cores gathers independently from its 16 connected partitions; OOB is undefined.
trigger: Gathering across the whole 128 partitions with a single index set.
fix: Replicate the index tile 8x across 16-partition groups; use nc_n_gather for within-partition gathers.
check_sketch: local_gather: index.dtype==uint16; shape[0]%16==0; num_elem_per_idx in {1,2,4,8,16,32}; indices per core <= 4096

rule: For nc_n_gather use uint32 indices in SBUF with the same partition count as data, dst dtype == data dtype, indices in [0, elems_per_partition); cost scales as ceil(elems/512) ISA groups.
why: GpSimd gathers within each partition over the flattened free dims; it avoids DMA entirely.
trigger: Using indirect dma_copy for in-SBUF gathers.
fix: nisa.nc_n_gather(dst, data, indices_u32).
check_sketch: nc_n_gather: indices.dtype==uint32; all sbuf; dst.dtype==data.dtype; prod(dst.shape[1:])==prod(indices.shape[1:])

rule: Call sequence_bounds with a partition dim of exactly 1 and fp32/int32 dtypes; output shape is (1, 2, N).
why: GpSimd segment scan is single-lane.
trigger: Passing (128,N) segment ids.
fix: Reshape so segment ids are (1,N).
check_sketch: sequence_bounds: segment_ids.shape[0]==1 and dtype in {fp32,int32}

rule: Use nisa.rng for integer-dtype random bits (Vector on trn1; Vector or GpSimd on trn2+), nisa.rand2 (trn3, Vector) for uniform floats, and seed with rand_set_state using 6 (GpSimd) or 24 (Vector) uint32 elements per partition.
why: Different PRNG implementations per engine with different state sizes; GpSimd outputs must be SBUF.
trigger: rand2 on trn2; rng into a float tile; rand_set_state with 1 element.
fix: Generate uint16 bits with rng then scale, or use nl.rand wrapper.
check_sketch: rng: dst.dtype int; rand2: nc_version>=4; rand_set_state: shape[1] in {6 (gpsimd), 24 (vector)}

rule: Rely on Vector/Scalar/GpSimd/DMA compute performing math in fp32 with a free cast to dst.dtype; do not add separate cast instructions.
why: All compute engines upcast inputs to fp32 and downcast on write at no extra cost (bitvec ops excepted).
trigger: tensor_copy casts inserted before/after arithmetic ops.
fix: Allocate dst in the desired dtype and let the op cast.
check_sketch: tensor_copy whose only purpose is a dtype change adjacent to an arithmetic op

rule: Use nl.float8_e4m3fn (OCP) only on trn3; on trn1/trn2 use legacy nl.float8_e4m3 (max 240) or set the UNSAFE_FP8FNCAST escape hatch for torch.float8_e4m3fn inputs.
why: The OCP e4m3fn datapath exists only on NeuronCore-v4; torch e4m3fn tensors are otherwise unrepresentable.
trigger: torch.float8_e4m3fn kernel inputs on trn2.
fix: Convert to nl.float8_e4m3 or bf16 before the kernel on trn2.
check_sketch: dtype float8_e4m3fn used with nc_version<4

rule: Request dtype=nl.uint8 (bool_) from comparison ops when the result feeds a predicate; nl.where expects float 1.0/0.0 conditions.
why: nl.bool_ is stored as uint8; comparison ops default to the input dtype.
trigger: Comparison result in bf16 passed as select_reduce predicate.
fix: mask = nl.greater(x, 0, dtype=nl.uint8).
check_sketch: predicate producer dtype is float
source: nki/api/nki.api.shared.rst dtype table; nl.not_equal and nl.where docstrings

rule: Avoid tfloat32 for activation bias, select_reduce on_true, and as a general storage type; use it only as a matmul operand precision.
why: tf32 is a PE-array compute format; several Vector/Scalar paths reject it.
trigger: bias tile declared tfloat32; select_reduce on tf32 scores.
fix: Store in fp32/bf16.
check_sketch: activation.bias.dtype != tfloat32; select_reduce.on_true.dtype != tfloat32

rule: Use nl.abs_max/nl.abs_min (and activate2 reduce_op abs_max/abs_min) only on trn3.
why: These ALU ops were added in NeuronCore-v4.
trigger: abs_max in an amax-quantization kernel for trn2.
fix: Compute abs then maximum on trn2.
check_sketch: op in {abs_max, abs_min} implies nc_version>=4

rule: Expect nki.simulate to model bf16/fp8 precisely by default (NKI_PRECISE_FP=1) and to reproduce hardware sin extrapolation; set NKI_PRECISE_FP=0 only to restore fp32 approximation.
why: Since 0.4.0 the CPU simulator defaults to precise low-precision emulation.
trigger: Simulator/hardware mismatches attributed to the kernel when they come from precision mode.
fix: Run NKI_SIMULATOR=1 or nki.simulate(kernel)(...) with default precision; compare with rtol per dtype.
source: migration/index.rst 0.3->0.4 'CPU simulator precision default'; nki.api.shared.rst act note

rule: Declare on-chip (SBUF/PSUM) tensors with the partition dimension as dim 0 (<=128) and never use block dimensions or nl.par_dim.
why: Block dimensions and par_dim were removed; dim 0 of every on-chip tensor maps to hardware partitions and view ops cannot move it.
trigger: nl.ndarray((8, nl.par_dim(128), 512)) or shapes whose first dim exceeds 128.
fix: Fold extra leading dims into the free dims ((128, 8, 512)) or use a Python list of (128, 512) tensors.
check_sketch: nl.ndarray(buffer in {sbuf,psum}): shape[0] <= 128; no nl.par_dim symbol (absent in 0.6.0)
source: nki.language.NkiTensor docstring 'Partition dimension'; migration/index.rst 'Removing block dimensions'

rule: On on-chip tensors use view ops only on free dims: permute keeps dims[0]==0, reshape keeps shape[0], flatten_dims start_dim>0, broadcast/expand_dim/squeeze_dim/reshape_dim dim != 0.
why: Partitions are physically separate memory banks, so a view cannot reinterpret the partition axis.
trigger: t.permute((1,0)) on an SBUF tile to 'transpose'; t.reshape((256, 64)) from (128,128).
fix: Use nc_transpose/dma_transpose for real transposes; keep shape[0] in reshape.
check_sketch: view op on sbuf/psum tensor: partition dim unchanged (dims[0]==0, new_shape[0]==shape[0], dim>0)

rule: Use t.view(dtype) for byte reinterpretation only when the last dim is contiguous and (for a larger dtype) divisible by the size ratio; not after dynamic/vector select.
why: view() rescales the last dim by the dtype size ratio without copying.
trigger: Viewing a strided slice as uint8; viewing (128, 3) uint8 as float32.
fix: Make the slice contiguous (tensor_copy) or pad the last dim.
check_sketch: view(): last dim stride==1 and (itemsize_new>itemsize_old -> shape[-1] % ratio == 0) and not is_indirect

rule: Ensure reshape preserves total element count; since 0.5.0 mismatches raise at trace time.
why: Earlier releases silently allowed count-changing reshapes.
trigger: Legacy kernels reshaping (128,512) to (128,256) to 'crop'.
fix: Use slice() for cropping and reshape only for layout changes.
check_sketch: reshape: prod(new)==prod(old)

rule: Use at most one dynamic select/vector_select per tensor; vector_select only on HBM tensors with dim 0; dynamic select on on-chip tensors may not target dim 0; the indirect dim cannot be further sliced or selected.
why: Dynamic indexing becomes a single indirect DMA descriptor dimension.
trigger: sbuf_t.select(0, idx_tensor); hbm_t.vector_select(0, idx).select(0, 3).
fix: Check t.is_indirect() before chaining; restructure gathers as one indirect DMA.
check_sketch: chain of dynamic selects on one tensor > 1; vector_select on non-hbm or dim!=0

rule: Use .indirect(index) (Tensor Indirection) only on trn3, with index an SBUF (P,K) tensor where P == tensor.shape[0]; when manually allocated the index starts on a 32-partition quadrant boundary and operands start on the same partition as their index.
why: TI reads/writes a column at per-element free offsets stored in a snake across partition groups (16 for vector/scalar/gpsimd, 32 for tensor engine).
trigger: indirect views on trn2; index at partition 16 for a tensor engine op.
fix: Gate on nc_version>=4; allocate index/operands with address=(0 or 32 or 64 or 96, ...).
check_sketch: indirect(): nc_version>=4 and index.shape[0]==self.shape[0] and buffer(index)==sbuf; manual address partition % 32 == 0

rule: Slice with 0 <= start < end <= shape[dim], step >= 1, and never slice a dimension participating in an indirection.
why: slice() is a strided view; invalid ranges fail at trace time, and indirect dims are opaque.
trigger: Negative or reversed slices; slicing the vector_select dim.
fix: Compute explicit bounds with min(); use Python slice objects for bounds-safe tiling.
check_sketch: slice(): 0<=start<end<=shape[dim] and step>=1 and dim not indirect

rule: Keep the sum of live SBUF tiles per partition under nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax_bytes (trn1 180224 B, trn2 212984 B, trn3 245752 B) and never exceed it with a single tile's free dim.
why: SBUF is 192/224/256 KiB per partition across 128 partitions (24/28/32 MiB total) minus 16 KiB reserved (plus 8 B on gen3/gen4); every instruction's elements-per-partition must fit the physical partition.
trigger: Large fp32 tiles (e.g. (128, 65536) fp32 = 256 KiB/partition) or too many double buffers failing allocation.
fix: Tile the free dim; use bf16 staging; read nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax_bytes inside the kernel for portable sizing.
check_sketch: nl.ndarray(sbuf): prod(shape[1:])*itemsize <= nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax_bytes(target)

rule: Plan PSUM usage as 8 banks x 2 KiB per partition (16 KiB total, 512 fp32 per bank); a manually addressed PSUM tensor must start at a bank boundary.
why: PSUM is the matmul accumulator memory; bank boundaries matter for accumulation groups and manual allocation errors otherwise.
trigger: address=(0, 1024) for a PSUM tile; more than 8 concurrent (128,512) fp32 accumulators.
fix: address=(0, bank_id*2048); limit live PSUM accumulators to psum_num_banks; evacuate promptly.
check_sketch: nl.ndarray(psum, address=(p,f)): f % 2048 == 0; live psum bytes per partition <= 16384

rule: Align manually chosen SBUF/PSUM free-dim byte offsets to at least 4 bytes (nl.tile_size.sbuf_min_align / psum_min_align).
why: Hardware address granularity for free-dim addressing is 4 bytes.
trigger: address=(0, 1) on a bf16 tile (2-byte offset).
fix: Round free offsets up to a multiple of 4 bytes (prefer larger, e.g. 64 B, for DMA efficiency).
check_sketch: nl.ndarray(address=(p,f)): f*itemsize % 4 == 0

rule: Use nl.tile_size.psum_bank_fmax and sbuf_fmax_bytes/sbuf_size_bytes instead of the deprecated psum_fmax and total_available_sbuf_size.
why: psum_fmax is misnamed (it is per bank, not per partition) and total_available_sbuf_size returns per-partition bytes despite its name.
trigger: Kernels computing PSUM budgets from psum_fmax * psum_num_banks or total SBUF from total_available_sbuf_size.
fix: Replace attribute names; multiply psum_bank_fmax by psum_num_banks for the whole PSUM.
check_sketch: attribute access tile_size.psum_fmax or tile_size.total_available_sbuf_size

rule: Read target-dependent constants (psum_num_banks, sbuf_fmax, sbuf_fmax_bytes, sbuf_size_bytes, get_nc_version) only inside a traced kernel or with a target set; at module import they raise 'No backend set'.
why: These are properties resolved from the compile target; the static ones (pmax, gemm_*_fmax, psum_bank_fmax, bn_stats_fmax) are plain ints.
trigger: Module-level constants like FMAX = nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax crashing at import.
fix: Compute inside the @nki.jit function or hard-code per target with NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE.
check_sketch: module-level access of tile_size.{psum_num_banks,sbuf_fmax,sbuf_fmax_bytes,sbuf_size_bytes,total_available_sbuf_size} or nisa.get_nc_version()
source: introspection: nl.tile_size property access raised RuntimeError('No backend set'); _tile_size.py

rule: Allocate kernel output (returned) tensors with buffer=nl.shared_hbm; nl.hbm/nl.private_hbm outputs fail compilation.
why: Returned tensors must be visible to the host and to both cores under LNC2.
trigger: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.hbm); return out.
fix: buffer=nl.shared_hbm.
check_sketch: returned tensor buffer == shared_hbm

rule: When hand-allocating, pass address=(partition_offset, free_offset) to nl.ndarray where free_offset is in elements of the tensor dtype and translated to bytes by the compiler.
why: The 0.2.0+ allocation API replaced the old sb_mod/block allocators; the compiler no longer rotates addresses you fix.
trigger: Modular/mod allocators from NKI 0.1.0; overlapping manual regions.
fix: Compute per-buffer offsets explicitly (e.g. base + (i % nbuf) * tile_bytes) in a Python list of tensors.

rule: Treat nl.affine_range, nl.sequential_range, nl.static_range and nl.range as deprecated aliases of Python range(): every static loop is fully unrolled; write plain range().
why: In NKI 0.6.0 there is no distinction between affine/sequential/static loops; the compiler unrolls and schedules the straight-line program.
trigger: Kernels relying on affine_range for 'parallel' semantics or sequential_range to 'force dependencies'.
fix: Use range(); express ordering with nl.no_reorder() or Kernel.with_schedule edges; keep trip counts bounded (unrolled code size).
check_sketch: call to nl.affine_range/sequential_range/static_range/nl.range

rule: Keep statically unrolled trip counts modest (product of nested static ranges in the hundreds, not tens of thousands) or move the outer loop to nl.fori_loop.
why: All range loops are fully unrolled into straight-line instructions, so instruction count and compile time grow linearly with total iterations.
trigger: Compile times of minutes or instruction-stream limits on large sequence/batch loops.
fix: Restructure to fewer, larger tiles; use fori_loop for large outer counts with register offsets.
check_sketch: product of static loop bounds > ~10k nc_matmul-equivalent instructions
source: inferred from affine_range docstring ('fully unrolled loop')

rule: Replace 'for i in nl.dynamic_range(reg)' with nl.fori_loop(lo, hi, body) and bare 'while reg:' with nl.while_loop(reg, body).
why: Both old constructs are deprecated in 0.6.0 and unsupported by the tracer frontend (registers have no value at trace time).
trigger: TypeError from int()/range() on a VirtualRegister; deprecation warnings.
fix: def body(i): ...; nl.fori_loop(0, reg, body); def wbody(r): ...; return r; nl.while_loop(reg, wbody).
check_sketch: use of nl.dynamic_range or Python while on VirtualRegister

rule: In fori_loop/while_loop keep the step a positive compile-time int, treat the loop register as read-only (use it via .ap(scalar_offset=i)), carry state through SBUF/HBM, declare tensors used after the loop outside the body, and never nest these loops in nl.no_reorder().
why: The body is compiled once into a sequencer branch loop; Python arithmetic on the register and tensors allocated inside the body are not visible outside.
trigger: idx = i*128 in Python; accumulators created inside body and read after.
fix: Pre-scale by setting pattern stride; allocate accumulators before the loop and update in place.
check_sketch: fori_loop: step is int > 0; body_fun returns None; no Python arithmetic on VirtualRegister; not inside no_reorder
source: nki.language.fori_loop and while_loop docstrings; migration/index.rst 'Rules for migrated loops'

rule: Budget at most 64 32-bit registers per engine sequencer for VirtualRegisters; register_load/register_store move single-element ([1] or [1,1]) tensors only.
why: Each of Tensor/Scalar/Vector/GpSimd/Sync sequencers has 64 scalar registers on NeuronCore v2-v4; the compiler allocates physical registers per engine.
trigger: Dozens of live loop registers; register_load from a (1,8) tile.
fix: Keep few live registers; materialize others to SBUF with register_store.
check_sketch: register_load/store: prod(src.shape)==1

rule: Wrap instruction sequences that must execute in program order in 'with nl.no_reorder():' (static loops allowed inside, register loops not).
why: The scheduler otherwise freely reorders independent instructions for engine utilization.
trigger: Accumulator-register chains or barrier/DMA ordering being reordered.
fix: with nl.no_reorder(): activation(reset_reduce); activation(reduce); ...
check_sketch: no_reorder block containing fori_loop/while_loop

rule: Add explicit scheduling dependencies with instruction name= tags and Kernel.with_schedule([(from_name, to_name_or_list), ...]) or instr.depends_on(other); the second tuple element must be a str or list, not a tuple.
why: with_schedule attaches dependency edges the scheduler must respect; names come from the name= kwarg on nisa calls.
trigger: Needing to delay a DMA until compute finishes without a data dependency.
fix: k = nki.jit(fn).with_schedule([('store_out', ['mm_last'])]); nisa.dma_copy(..., name='store_out').
check_sketch: with_schedule edge second element is tuple

rule: Leave address rotation enabled (default) so multi-buffered tensors rotate addresses; disable with Kernel.disable_address_rotation() only when manual addresses must be stable.
why: Address rotation lets the compiler give loop-iteration copies of a tensor different physical addresses, enabling overlap.
trigger: Debugging with manual addresses while rotation moves buffers.
fix: kernel = nki.jit(fn).disable_address_rotation().

rule: Declare per-iteration SBUF tiles inside the loop body (not once outside) so the compiler can multi-buffer them; reuse one outer tensor only when iterations must serialize.
why: A single tensor reused across iterations carries a loop dependency that serializes load/compute/store; a fresh declaration per iteration lets unrolled copies overlap.
trigger: Load->compute->store pipelines running serially in the profile.
fix: for i in range(n): buf = nl.ndarray((128,512), ...); dma_copy(buf,...); ...
check_sketch: sbuf tensor declared before a loop and both written and read in every iteration
source: migration/index.rst 'If blocks do not need to be alive at the same time' (warning)

rule: When several tiles must be alive simultaneously, allocate one tensor with the block count folded into a free dim ((128, 8, 512)) or a Python list of tensors.
why: Block dimensions were removed; a list or a folded free dim gives the compiler the same liveness information.
trigger: Reductions over 8 loaded tiles after the load loop.
fix: add_buf = nl.ndarray((128, 8, 512)); add_buf[:, i, :] used per iteration.
source: migration/index.rst 'Use a Python-like list' / 'move the block dimension into the free dimension'

rule: Launch LNC2 kernels as kernel[2](args) and keep that degree equal to NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG; default is LNC=1.
why: The bracket syntax sets the kernel's logical core count; a mismatch with the runtime configuration is a runtime error.
trigger: kernel(args) under NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2.
fix: Use kernel[lnc](...) and nki.simulate(kernel[2]) for simulation.
check_sketch: Kernel.lnc != env NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG

rule: Shard work across the two physical cores with nl.program_id(0)/nl.num_programs(0), launching with an SPMD grid equal to the LNC degree; expect future releases to specialize across PNCs automatically and reject mismatched grids.
why: Under LNC2 each physical NeuronCore runs the same program with a different program_id.
trigger: SPMD grid size differing from the LNC degree.
fix: core = nl.program_id(0); process rows [core*half:(core+1)*half].
check_sketch: SPMD grid dims == lnc
source: nki.language.program_id/num_programs docstrings; migration/index.rst 'Deprecation notice: SPMD launch grid'

rule: Insert nisa.core_barrier(data=shared_tensor, cores=(0,1)) after each core writes its part of a shared HBM tensor and before any core reads the other's part (trn2+, LNC2 only).
why: Cores run asynchronously; the barrier exchanges semaphores so reads see completed writes. Only cores=(0,1) and shared-HBM data are supported; it blocks only the chosen engine (default GpSimd).
trigger: Stale/zero halves of a shared tensor read by the peer core.
fix: dma_copy(shared[half], ...); core_barrier(shared, (0,1)); then read.
check_sketch: LNC2 kernel: shared_hbm tensor written by one program_id and read by another without core_barrier between

rule: Compile LNC2 kernels with Kernel.enable_core_barrier_checker() during development to fail compilation on cross-PNC races.
why: The checker compares all memory accesses across the two PNCs and reports write/read overlaps lacking a barrier on a common engine.
trigger: Intermittent wrong results in LNC2 kernels.
fix: kernel = nki.jit(fn).enable_core_barrier_checker(); disable for production builds.

rule: Use nisa.sendrecv only between ranks 0 and 1 with SBUF src/dst of identical dtype/shape; with dma_engine.gpsimd_dma keep per-partition payload <= 1024 B (32-bit), 512 B (16-bit), 256 B (8-bit); group operations with pipe_id.
why: sendrecv swaps SBUF tiles between the two cores sharing an HBM stack; the GpSimd DMA path is low latency but size limited.
trigger: sendrecv of a (128, 1024) bf16 tile over gpsimd_dma (2048 B/partition).
fix: Split into chunks or use dma_engine.dma.
check_sketch: sendrecv: buffers sbuf; same dtype/shape; ranks in {0,1}; gpsimd_dma -> bytes_per_partition <= 1024/512/256 by itemsize

rule: Keep nl.shared_constant data identical for both cores under LNC2 and use only the supported element types (fp32/fp16/bf16/int*/uint*/fp8_e4m3fn/fp8_e5m2/e8m0fnu).
why: Constants are embedded in the NEFF and loaded once to shared HBM.
trigger: Per-core constant tables; packed/tfloat32 constants (untested on hardware).
fix: Index into one shared table with program_id.
check_sketch: shared_constant dtype in supported set

rule: Debug device/simulator mismatches with nki.debug(kernel, dump_dir=NEURON_RT_DEBUG_OUTPUT_DIR)(args) and breakpoint() in the kernel; for LNC2 both cores run as threads and only core_id stops.
why: nki.debug replays the kernel in simulation while loading device dumps for tensor.sim_value vs device_value comparison.
trigger: Hardware NaNs not reproduced in nki.simulate.
fix: Set NEURON_RT_DEBUG_OUTPUT_DIR on the device run, then nki.debug(..., interactive=True).

rule: Give each collective tensors all in HBM or all in SBUF; coalesced (multi-tensor) collectives require HBM.
why: The collective engines treat HBM and SBUF transfers differently and cannot mix them in one op.
trigger: all_reduce(srcs=[hbm_t, sbuf_t], ...).
fix: Stage to one memory space; pass a single tensor for SBUF collectives.
check_sketch: collective: all buffers equal; len(srcs)>1 -> buffers hbm

rule: Use collective_dim=0 for HBM all_gather/reduce_scatter/all_to_all; for SBUF all_gather 0 or 1 is allowed but only on 2-D tensors with a single free dim.
why: Concatenation/splitting is implemented along the leading dim; SBUF collectives are 2-D only.
trigger: all_gather on a 3-D SBUF tile or collective_dim=1 on HBM.
fix: Reshape to put the gathered dim first.
check_sketch: collective_dim==0 unless (buffer==sbuf and ndim==2)

rule: Keep all_to_all, all_to_all_v, all_gather_v and collective_permute tensors in HBM; collective_permute takes exactly one tensor per list.
why: SBUF variants are not implemented for these ops.
trigger: collective_permute(srcs=[sbuf_tile], ...).
fix: dma_copy to an HBM staging tensor first.
check_sketch: op in {all_to_all, all_to_all_v, all_gather_v, collective_permute}: buffers hbm; collective_permute len(srcs)==1

rule: Use only nl.add, nl.minimum or nl.maximum as the reduction op for all_reduce/reduce_scatter/collective_permute_implicit_reduce.
why: Collective reduction hardware supports sum/min/max only.
trigger: op=nl.multiply in all_reduce.
fix: Reduce locally with log/exp tricks or do products on-core.
check_sketch: collective op in {add, minimum, maximum}

rule: For all_to_all_v/all_gather_v supply a uint32 metadata tensor shaped (rows, group_size) in HBM or (1, rows, group_size) in SBUF on one partition, rows=3 without rdispls or 4 with; row 2 (recv_counts) is written by the op unless recv_counts_known=True.
why: Per-rank counts/displacements are read at execution time from the metadata rows.
trigger: int32 metadata, or reading recv counts before the op completes.
fix: meta = nl.ndarray((3, G), nl.uint32, buffer=nl.shared_hbm) with rows send_counts/send_displs/recv_counts.
check_sketch: metadata.dtype==uint32 and shape matches rows x group_size

rule: Expect all_gather_v to require LNC=2 with 4-rank intra-chip subgroups and no rdispls, and all_to_all_v on NeuronSwitch instances to require LNC=2, >1 device, and rank lists that include all 4 ranks of each participating device (set send_count=0 to exclude).
why: Current runtime support for variable-length collectives is limited to these topologies.
trigger: all_to_all_v under LNC=1 or with partial-device rank lists.
fix: Restructure replica groups as sequential 4-rank lists per device.
check_sketch: all_gather_v: lnc==2 and len(rank_list)==4 and not has_rdispls

rule: Use at most 4 channels for replica groups covering all devices in a node and 2 otherwise; channel_ids must be consecutive integers starting at 0.
why: Channel count is bounded by system connectivity; each channel carries one tensor per list.
trigger: channel_ids=[1,2] or 6 channels.
fix: channel_ids=list(range(n)) with n<=4.
check_sketch: channel_ids == list(range(len(channel_ids))) and len<=4

rule: For ring communication use collective_permute_implicit (+ collective_permute_implicit_current_processing_rank_id) instead of explicit collective_permute pairs.
why: Hardware optimizes the implicit ring pattern and the rank id register lets compute overlap communication via dynamic .ap() offsets.
trigger: Explicit source_target_pairs building a ring.
fix: Loop over iterations: rank = ..._current_processing_rank_id(it, rg); use register ALU to compute chunk offset.
check_sketch: collective_permute with pairs forming (i, i+1 mod n)

rule: Define ReplicaGroup sub-groups as non-overlapping rank lists.
why: Overlapping groups make collective membership ambiguous.
trigger: Rank appearing in two sub-lists.
fix: Partition ranks exactly once.
check_sketch: ReplicaGroup lists pairwise disjoint

rule: Import nki, nki.language as nl, nki.isa as nisa, nki.collectives; never import neuronxcc.nki.* inside kernels.
why: The legacy namespace raises a compilation error since NKI 0.4.0 (the package is still importable but is the old 0.1.0 API).
trigger: from neuronxcc import nki / import neuronxcc.nki.language as nl.
fix: Replace imports; follow the 0.1->0.2 migration (dst-first ISA calls, no mask/mgrid/arange).
check_sketch: import of neuronxcc.nki
source: migration/index.rst 'neuronxcc.nki.* inside kernels - now a compilation error'

rule: Call every nisa instruction with dst as the first (explicit) argument; instructions return an NkiInstruction handle, not the result tile.
why: Since 0.2.0 ISA APIs write into a pre-allocated destination to avoid hidden copies and to express accumulation.
trigger: out = nisa.tensor_tensor(a, b, nl.add) / result[...] = nisa.reciprocal(x).
fix: nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=out, data1=a, data2=b, op=nl.add).
check_sketch: nisa.* call result assigned to a tensor or used as operand
source: migration/index.rst 'All ISA functions require a destination parameter'

rule: Do not use nl.mgrid, nl.arange or the mask= parameter; use integer slices (with min()) and .ap() for strided/dynamic patterns.
why: These 0.1.0 indexing mechanisms were removed; slicing covers in-bounds tiling.
fix: p = slice(i*128, min(N, (i+1)*128)); nisa.tensor_copy(dst[p, f], src[p, f]).
check_sketch: use of nl.mgrid/nl.arange/mask kwarg

rule: Pass enum members (nisa.dge_mode.hwdge, nisa.engine.vector, nl.sbuf) rather than ints or strings for dge_mode/engine/oob_mode/reduce_cmd/buffer parameters.
why: Raw integer enum values and string buffer names are rejected since 0.3.0.
trigger: dge_mode=2, buffer='sbuf'.
fix: Use the named members; nl.ndarray buffer defaults to nl.sbuf.
check_sketch: enum kwarg is int or buffer kwarg is str

rule: Do not pass platform_target= or mode= to @nki.jit; set NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE (trn1|inf2|gen2, trn2|gen3, trn3|gen4) and let argument types select torch/jax/numpy execution.
why: platform_target raises since 0.3.0 and mode is ignored; framework is detected from args.
trigger: @nki.jit(platform_target='trn2', mode='baremetal').
fix: @nki.jit plus env var; nki.simulate for CPU runs.
check_sketch: nki.jit kwargs contain platform_target or mode

rule: Do not call nki.benchmark, nki.baremetal or nki.profile (absent in 0.6.0); run with @nki.jit on numpy inputs, nki.simulate for CPU, nki.compiler.parallel_compile for batch builds, and neuron-profile for timing.
why: The 0.1.0 decorators were dropped with the new compiler; nki exposes jit, simulate, debug, Kernel, compiler.
trigger: AttributeError: module 'nki' has no attribute 'benchmark'.
fix: Replace with nki.jit + external timing / neuron-profile.
